posts.title: Celebrating ten years of Svelte
posts.description: It started with a commit — specifically, this one . Ten years later, we’re far from done; software never is. But we’ve come an awful long way. Last week the community gathered in Ljubljana, at the third in-person Svelte Summit , to mark the anniversary. One of several cakes that were eaten at the conference To be completely honest, I expected the atmosphere to be a little subdued. Being enthusiastic about front end frameworks feels somewhat passé in the era of agentic coding and software factories, so a conference dedicated to one of the more boutique ones could easily have felt like a bit of a throwback. But I was wrong. The energy was fantastic. We had two days of lively conversation and unbelievable demos in one of Europe’s most beautiful cities, with a slew of announcements that we’ll follow up on in more detail soon: Custom renderers are now supported behind an experimental flag, allowing you to use Svelte to build native apps and terminal UIs and PDFs and just about anything else

posts.title: What’s new in Svelte: October 2026
posts.description: SvelteKit 3 is here! Check out the announcement post for the highlights, then run sv migrate to handle most of the upgrade for you. sv itself hit 1.0 on the same day, making the community add-on API official. Below you’ll find the last round of changes that landed before 3.0 - adapter API updates, zero-config deploys to Render and a few final breaking changes. Svelte Summit is also back for Svelte’s 10th birthday! It’s happening in Ljubljana on November 19-20 with talks from Rich Harris, Elliott Johnson, Paolo Ricciuti, Stanislav Khromov, pngwn and more. In-person and virtual tickets are available at sveltesummit.com . Svelte itself had a quiet month - 5.57.1 is all bug fixes and parser performance work. Per usual, there’s still plenty in the showcase... so let’s dive in! What’s new in SvelteKit 3 Adapters now receive the Svelte config as a function argument when adding Vite plugins ( 3.0.0-next.27 , #16986 ) Adapters can override getRequest and setResponse during vite dev and vite pre

posts.title: SvelteKit 3 is here
posts.description: Version 3.0 of SvelteKit, the official application framework for Svelte, is now available. If you’ve used earlier versions of SvelteKit, everything will feel very familiar — it’s the same framework with a little more polish, a little more type safety, and a little less junk. We’ve made migration as seamless as we can with the sv migrate command... npx sv migrate sveltekit - 3 -- tasks all -- confirm ...which will automatically migrate as much of your codebase as possible, and generate a TODO list for everything else. (If you’re agentically inclined, your robot friends will make short work of it.) To create a new app, run sv create : npx sv create my - new - app As with any major version bump there are a handful of breaking changes to be aware of, which are covered in the migration guide (or, more briefly, in the recent release candidate announcement ). Quick highlights: configuration now lives in vite.config.ts instead of svelte.config.js the $lib alias is now #lib , making use of stan
